overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a member who received a private public-caller question and declined to repeat it did not have to disclose it, and remote participation rules apply only to members, not the public.

allegations.summary: Board took public questions by phone during the Ask the Selectmen portion but a member did not repeat one caller's question to the audience.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not discuss the topic, the single member who received the call was not required to disclose the question to the public, and did not violate the law by failing to do so.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to follow proper remote participation procedures when taking questions from members of the public by telephone.
allegations.key_passage: The procedures for remote participation outlined in the Attorney General's Regulations, 940 CMR 29.10, apply only to members of public bodies who wish to participate in meetings remotely.
